summary: Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, seeking a third term, leads Democratic state Rep. Gina Hinojosa by low single digits in most October polls, with Emerson at 49 to 45, though a few surveys show Hinojosa narrowly ahead. The race centers on property taxes, affordability and public schools, with Abbott declining to debate and Hinojosa suing over his office's emails with Elon Musk.

issues.why: A 12 million dollar Abbott ad buy says Hinojosa voted more than 40 times for higher property taxes, which she denies, while she says ending corporate welfare could cut them.
Hinojosa would fire Education Commissioner Mike Morath and pause A through F ratings, while Abbott pledges to make Texas first in public education.
Hinojosa proposes returning rainy day fund money above 10 billion dollars, about 1,500 dollars per household, and Abbott runs an affordability agenda tour.
Abbott, backed by the National Border Patrol Council and police groups, calls Hinojosa soft on crime and illegal immigration.
Analysts say the data center boom and economic worries are headwinds for Republicans, and Abbott pledges more energy market competition.

storylines.title: Emerson poll has Abbott up 4
storylines.what: Emerson found Abbott at 49 and Hinojosa at 45 among likely voters, with Hinojosa gaining but Abbott still favored.

storylines.title: Hinojosa sues over Musk emails
storylines.what: Hinojosa sued in Travis County for unredacted emails between Abbott's office and Elon Musk, and Abbott's campaign called it a baseless act of desperation and said it handed over all required records.

storylines.title: Labor and teachers back Hinojosa
storylines.what: Hinojosa has the Texas AFL-CIO and Texas AFT, while Abbott has Trump and major police and border agent groups.

storylines.title: Empty lectern at the Governor's Mansion
storylines.what: Hinojosa staged a debate with an empty podium for Abbott, who was with East Texas law enforcement and said showing up in communities matters most.

storylines.title: Polls tighten through October
storylines.what: A UT Texas Politics Project poll had Hinojosa up 49 to 48 while most other October polls showed Abbott ahead by 1 to 5 points.

storylines.title: Abbott ramps up attacks
storylines.what: Abbott launched a 12 million dollar property tax ad and posted an altered image accusing Hinojosa of wanting gender transition camps in schools.

events.title: Debate or no debate
events.prompt: The challenger has accepted four debate invitations and the governor has declined them all. What does the campaign do?

opts.label: Empty podium stunt
opts.say: Stage a debate outside the mansion and say he cannot defend his record.

opts.label: Agree to one debate
opts.say: Accept a single televised debate to settle the question and return to issues.

opts.label: Stay on the road
opts.say: Skip debates and keep meeting voters with local police and community leaders.

events.title: Property tax votes
events.prompt: A 12 million dollar ad says the Democrat voted over 40 times for higher property taxes, which she calls out of context. What is the property tax message?

opts.label: End corporate welfare
opts.say: Cut property taxes by ending corporate tax breaks and refund the rainy day surplus.

opts.label: Targeted relief
opts.say: Raise homestead exemptions and cap appraisals without big new programs.

opts.label: Eliminate school taxes
opts.say: Use state money to wipe out local school property taxes and require votes on tax hikes.

events.title: Musk emails
events.prompt: A lawsuit seeks the governor's office emails with Elon Musk, whose PAC is spending heavily in Texas races. How does the campaign play it?

opts.label: Billionaire influence
opts.say: Argue Texas is run for billionaires and demand full release of the emails.

opts.label: Transparency pledge
opts.say: Promise faster public records responses for any governor without leveling charges.

opts.label: Call it desperation
opts.say: Dismiss the suit as a stunt and tout Musk companies moving jobs to Texas.

events.title: School leadership
events.prompt: Parents are frustrated with state school ratings and leadership. What is the education plan?

opts.label: Fire the commissioner
opts.say: Replace the education commissioner on day one and pause A through F ratings.

opts.label: Raise teacher pay
opts.say: Focus on teacher pay and classroom funding while keeping accountability.

opts.label: Parents first
opts.say: Defend school choice and accuse the opponent of pushing gender ideology in schools.

ads.theme: A 12 million dollar buy saying Hinojosa voted more than 40 times for higher property taxes.
Social media ad warning Don't let Gina deceive you, Texas.
